$schema_notes: Machine-readable Laravel-vs-vi/validation compatibility matrix. One entry per Vi\Validation\Rules\RuleId case, keyed by its canonical rule-string name, plus a few notable aliases (ipv4/ipv6) whose behavior diverges from their canonical rule. status: full = pass/fail and failed-field parity verified for the mainstream grammar; partial = parity holds except for a documented exception (see notes); divergent = currently/intentionally not Laravel-compatible, current behavior pinned by an assertDivergence() test; not_applicable = no directly comparable Laravel rule (tested for internal correctness only, not cross-validated). native_compilable reflects Vi\Validation\Compilation\NativeCompiler::isSupported() for the rule's class. Every 'full'/'partial' entry must be referenced by name in at least one tests/Unit/Parity/*ParityTest.php file; every 'divergent' entry must have a non-empty notes string and a matching assertDivergence() call. Enforced by tests/Unit/Parity/CompatibilityMatrixTest.php.

_attribute_addressing.notes: Depth-2 dot nesting ('parent.child') has full parity with Laravel for every rule. Depth-3+ nesting ('a.b.c') and wildcard segments ('items.*.sku') are not implemented anywhere in CompiledField/ValidatorEngine: a wildcard or 3+-level field name never resolves against real data, so implicit rules (e.g. required) on it fail unconditionally and non-implicit rules silently no-op, regardless of Laravel's per-index expansion. Pinned by tests/Unit/Parity/NestedWildcardParityTest.php via assertDivergence().

required_if_accepted.notes: LaravelRuleParser had no case for this rule string (crashed with ArgumentCountError); fixed as part of issue #5.

missing_if.notes: Laravel supports multiple dependent values (missing_if:field,val1,val2). MissingIfRule's constructor only accepts one value; LaravelRuleParser (fixed for the crash in issue #5) wires only the first value. Multi-value parity not implemented.

missing_with.notes: LaravelRuleParser previously built this with zero fields (variadic ctor, silent no-op); fixed as part of issue #5.

prohibits.notes: LaravelRuleParser previously built this with zero fields (variadic ctor, silent no-op); fixed as part of issue #5.

exclude_if.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (no case in LaravelRuleParser). Fixed for the crash, but same single-value limitation as missing_if: Laravel's multi-value dependent form is not supported.

exclude_unless.notes: Same fix and same single-value limitation as exclude_if.

exclude_with.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (no case in LaravelRuleParser); fixed.

exclude_without.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (no case in LaravelRuleParser); fixed.

accepted_if.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5. Fixed for the crash, but AcceptedIfRule only supports one dependent value where Laravel supports multiple.

declined_if.notes: Same fix and same single-value limitation as accepted_if. Also fixed as part of issue #5: was missing from ValidatorEngine/NativeCompiler's implicit-rule whitelists (see 'declined').

enum.notes: Laravel has no native 'enum:ClassName' string-rule grammar (Enum is normally applied as a Rule object). The parity test passes an equivalent [new Illuminate\Validation\Rules\Enum(...)] to Laravel and the string form to Fast rather than sharing one rules array; underlying validation semantics match. Rule string previously crashed (no case in LaravelRuleParser); fixed as part of issue #5.

decimal.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (no case in LaravelRuleParser); fixed.

ipv4.notes: Known bug, not fixed by issue #5: LaravelRuleParser has no case for the 'ipv4' alias, so it falls through to `new IpRule()` with no version restriction, silently behaving like plain 'ip' instead of rejecting IPv6 addresses like Laravel does.

ipv6.notes: Same bug as ipv4: the alias loses its version restriction and behaves like plain 'ip'.

digits_between.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (LaravelRuleParser cast params to float, but DigitsBetweenRule's constructor requires int); fixed.

distinct.notes: Different grammar, same semantics: Laravel validates per-element via wildcard ('tags.*' => 'distinct'); vi/validation's DistinctRule validates the whole array directly ('tags' => 'array|distinct') since wildcards aren't implemented. Compared via assertEquivalentParity() in ArrayParityTest, not a byte-identical rules array. Also fixed as part of issue #5: 'strict' mode used array_unique(..., SORT_REGULAR), which is still loose comparison (1 == '1'), so it never actually matched Laravel's ===-based in_array($value,$data,true) check; replaced with a real strict-equality pass.

required_array_keys.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (RequiredArrayKeysRule takes variadic string ...$keys, but LaravelRuleParser wrongly grouped it with array-taking rules like required_with); fixed.

mimetypes.notes: LaravelRuleParser previously built this with zero types (MimetypesRule takes variadic string ...$types, but was wrongly grouped with array-taking 'mimes'; silent no-op); fixed as part of issue #5.

extensions.notes: Two fixes as part of issue #5: (1) LaravelRuleParser previously built this with zero extensions (variadic ctor, silent no-op). (2) ExtensionsRule compared the extension of the file's real temp path ('/tmp/phpXXXXXX', no extension) instead of the uploaded file's original client filename, so it always failed for real uploads; now prefers getClientOriginalExtension() when available, matching Laravel's validateExtensions().

min_file_size.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (no case in LaravelRuleParser; only max_file_size was handled). Fixed. Different rule name than Laravel, same semantics: Laravel overloads 'min:N' to mean kilobytes when the value is a File instance; vi/validation gives it a distinct name. Compared via assertEquivalentParity() in FileParityTest ('file|min:N' vs 'file|min_file_size:N').

max_file_size.notes: Same as min_file_size: Laravel overloads 'max:N'; vi/validation names it separately. Compared via assertEquivalentParity().

dimensions.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (no case in LaravelRuleParser); fixed with a key=value constraint parser (min_width, max_width, min_height, max_height, width, height, ratio).

declined.notes: Fixed as part of issue #5: ValidatorEngine/NativeCompiler's implicit-rule whitelists included AcceptedRule but not DeclinedRule, so 'declined' silently passed when the field was entirely missing instead of failing like Laravel does.

exists.notes: Crashed via rule string before issue #5 (no case in LaravelRuleParser). Fixed with the full table/column/connection/extra-where grammar. Not supported: referencing an Eloquent model class as the table parameter (requires resolving a real model at parse time, which this standalone parser does not do). SEPARATE, UNFIXED GAP: Vi\Validation\Laravel\FastValidatorFactory never wires a DatabaseValidatorInterface into the ValidatorEngine it builds and has no config option to supply one, so exists/unique used through FastValidator::make() always silently pass regardless of real data. DatabaseParityTest exercises the rule classes directly via SchemaValidator/ValidatorEngine (which does support setDatabaseValidator()) rather than through FastValidatorFactory.

unique.notes: Same fix as exists, plus ignore-id/id-column/extra-where grammar. Not supported: the `[field]` bracket syntax for a per-row dynamic ignore id (requires resolving the value from ValidationContext at validate-time, not parse-time) and the Eloquent-model-class table form. Same FastValidatorFactory DatabaseValidatorInterface wiring gap as exists - see its notes.

country.notes: vi/validation-only extension; Laravel has no built-in 'country' rule to compare against. Tested for internal correctness only, not cross-validated.

language.notes: vi/validation-only extension; Laravel has no built-in 'language' rule to compare against. Tested for internal correctness only, not cross-validated.

conditional.notes: Internal mechanism behind FieldDefinition::when(), never a user-typed rule-string name. Its Laravel-equivalent behavior (Illuminate's Validator::sometimes()/conditional closures) is exercised functionally in tests/Unit/Parity/ClosureParityTest.php rather than compared as a standalone named rule.

closure.notes: Internal wrapper for user-supplied Laravel-style closures, never a user-typed rule-string name. Exercised functionally in tests/Unit/Parity/ClosureParityTest.php. Fixed as part of issue #5: SchemaValidator::validate() crashed (Exception: Serialization of 'Closure' is not allowed) on every call for any schema containing an inline closure rule, because NativeCompiler::generateKey() ran a plain serialize() on the raw rules array for its native-cache-lookup key. This made the documented closure-rule feature entirely unusable via SchemaValidator::validate() (and therefore FastValidator too). generateKey() now falls back to a closure-safe normalization on serialize() failure.
